The sea floor: depth in colour, its relief, and depth contours

Source: R/relief.R
og_relief.Rd

og_relief() draws a depth model as two layers: the depth in colour, and its relief shaded. og_contour() draws lines of equal depth from the same model: the chart depths (major) a little heavier and labelled, thinner lines between them, spaced by depth and zoom. Both are made in the page from the model's tiles of elevations, so the reader changes the colours, the shading and the lines with nothing asked of R; a bundle (og_bundle()) carries them with no R at all. Each draws under the base map's place names, whatever its place in the pipe.

Usage

og_relief(
  map = NULL,
  tiles = NULL,
  palette = "grey",
  opacity = 75,
  limits = NULL,
  scale = NULL,
  shade = TRUE,
  of = c("depth", "elevation"),
  open = FALSE,
  name = "Depth",
  id = "depth",
  info = NULL,
  section = "Sea floor",
  visible = TRUE
)

og_contour(
  map = NULL,
  tiles = NULL,
  major = c(10, 25, 50, 100, 150, 200, 300, 400, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3000, 4000,
    5000),
  minor = TRUE,
  labels = TRUE,
  colour = "#1b2a3a",
  of = c("depth", "elevation"),
  open = FALSE,
  name = "Contours",
  id = "contours",
  info = NULL,
  section = "Sea floor",
  visible = TRUE
)

Arguments

map

A map the pipe makes (og_map(), with data or none, and any layer functions). Given the depth model instead (or nothing), a map is started for it, opening on the model's extent.

tiles

The depth model (see The depth model).

palette

The colours' look, one of the map's palettes: by default "grey", quiet under the map's own data; "quiet", "seabed", "deep", "chart", "drained" and "haxby" are the other depth looks (og_palettes()).

opacity

The colours' opacity, 0-100.

limits

The depths (or heights) the palette's ends stand at, c(floor, cap) in metres from 1 to 10,000; by default fitted to the view, again each time the map settles (the 2nd and 98th percentiles of the values in view), until the reader sets them.

scale

How the values are spread over the palette: "log", "linear", or "equal" (each colour an equal share of the values in view); by default equal shares.

shade

The relief shaded, as a layer of its own: TRUE, at an intensity that follows the view; a number from 0 to 1, that intensity; or FALSE, none.

of

"depth" (below sea level, what is above left clear) or "elevation" (on land).

open

Whether the layers' controls show when the page opens; folded by default.

name, info

The layer's name in the sidebar (the relief's is "Relief") and the text behind its ⓘ.

id

The layer's id, its key in the page's address; the relief's is <id>_relief.

section

The sidebar's box the layers sit in, by its title.

visible

Whether the layers are on when the page opens.

major

The depths (or heights) of the heavier, labelled lines, in metres; by default the charts' isobaths from 10 to 5,000 m. Each shows from the zoom at which the thinner lines are no wider apart than it is deep.

minor

Whether thinner lines are drawn between the major ones: every 25 m on the shelf at zoom 5, every 5 m from zoom 10, wider apart in deeper water (bands at 50, 200 and 1,000 m) and further out.

labels

Whether the major lines carry their depth.

colour

The lines' and labels' colour, "#rrggbb".

Value

The map, with the layers.

Details

The arguments are the starting look; the page's controls change it. They open folded under the layer's name, a click on ▸ showing them (open = TRUE shows them from the start); the colours' scale bar shows either way.

The depth model

tiles is the depth model, one of:

  • nothing (NULL): the file named by the environment variable OGIS_DEPTH, a line in .Renviron (OGIS_DEPTH=D:/data/depth.mbtiles; og_tiles_mbtiles() says more), so a script shared between colleagues carries no path;

  • the path of an MBTiles file of elevation tiles, read by og_tiles_mbtiles();

  • a grid: the path of a GeoTIFF or any grid GDAL reads, a terra SpatRaster, or a data frame of cells, made into tiles by og_tiles_dem() (to zoom 8 by default);

  • a tile function already made, by og_tiles_mbtiles() or og_tiles_dem(); give the same one to both functions for a grid in a data frame, so a bundle holds its tiles once.

Elevations are metres, negative below sea level, as both tile functions give them.

See also

og_tiles_mbtiles() and og_tiles_dem() for the depth model; og_layer() for a layer in MapLibre's own terms.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("png", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # the Danish waters' depth, its relief and contours, under the harbours
  depth <- og_tiles_dem(og_example("dansk_relief"), maxzoom = 6)
  og_map(view = list(bounds = c(2.5, 54.5, 13, 58.5))) |>
    og_relief(depth) |>
    og_contour(depth) |>
    og_polygon(og_example("dansk_harbours"), fill = NA, name = "Harbours")

  # a depth model named once, by OGIS_DEPTH in .Renviron:
  # og_map() |> og_relief() |> og_contour()
}
#> <og_map> Map
#>   layers: depth (dem), depth_relief (dem), contours (contour), harbours (geojson)
# }
